questions.def: Use 'an' before a vowel sound to introduce the appositive phrase.
questions.question: My brother, ___ engineer, works in London.

questions.def: Use 'the' to specify the capital, acting as an appositive.
questions.question: Paris, ___ capital of France, is a beautiful city.

questions.def: 'Worker' is the correct noun to describe the person's job.
questions.question: My sister, a ___ for a big company, travels a lot.

questions.def: Use 'a' before a consonant sound to introduce the appositive phrase.
questions.question: My dog, ___ golden retriever, loves to play fetch.

questions.def: The appositive needs a determiner like 'our' to specify which teacher.
questions.question: Mr. Smith, ___ teacher, is very popular.

questions.def: 'Singer' is the correct noun to describe the person's profession.
questions.question: My mom, a talented ___, performs in local concerts.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'ancient' because it starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: Rome, ___ ancient city, attracts many tourists.

questions.def: The subject 'football' is singular, so use 'is'.
questions.question: My favorite sport, football, ___ very exciting.

questions.def: 'Cook' is the noun form for someone who cooks professionally.
questions.question: My uncle, a professional ___, owns a restaurant.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'kind' because it starts with a consonant sound.
questions.question: My best friend, ___ kind person, always helps others.

questions.def: 'The' specifies which city is being referred to.
questions.question: London, ___ city I love, is expensive.

questions.def: 'Driver' is the correct noun form.
questions.question: My neighbor, a careful ___, always obeys traffic rules.

questions.def: Use 'a' because 'playful' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.question: My cat, ___ playful animal, loves to chase toys.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce the appositive phrase.
questions.question: John, ___ student in my class, is very smart.

questions.def: 'Dancer' is the noun form of the person's profession.
questions.question: My friend, a graceful ___, performs ballet.

questions.def: Use 'an' because 'amazing' starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My aunt, ___ amazing cook, makes delicious cakes.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce the appositive phrase.
questions.question: My hometown, ___ small village, is very peaceful.

questions.def: 'Writer' is the noun form for someone who writes books.
questions.question: My cousin, a famous ___, has published many books.

questions.def: Using 'the' to specify which model the phone is.
questions.question: My phone, ___ new model, has a great camera.

questions.def: Use 'an' before 'old' as it starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My neighbor, ___ old man, is very friendly.

questions.def: 'Painter' is the correct noun for a person who paints.
questions.question: My uncle, a talented ___, sells his art.

questions.def: Use 'the' to specify which bike.
questions.question: My bike, ___ red one, needs some repairs.

questions.def: The subject 'Mrs. Jones' is singular, so use 'is'.
questions.question: My teacher, Mrs. Jones, ___ very helpful.

questions.def: The verb agrees with 'brother' (singular). Apposition doesn't change verb agreement.
questions.question: My brother, a doctor, ___ at the hospital.

questions.def: Use 'the' before a specific noun in apposition.
questions.question: Paris, ___ capital of France, is a beautiful city.

questions.def: Using present participle to add extra information.
questions.question: My aunt, ___ in London, is a teacher.

questions.def: 'Which is' introduces non-essential information about the dog.
questions.question: My dog, ___ small and fluffy, loves to play.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific capital city.
questions.question: I want to visit Rome, ___ capital of Italy.

questions.def: Using past participle as adjective in apposition.
questions.question: My neighbor, ___ Mr. Smith, is very kind.

questions.def: 'Which' is correct for non-restrictive relative clauses modifying things.
questions.question: My car, ___ is very old, still runs well.
